<!-- Generated by Kora's design director. This is the design decision the site was built
     from. Business: Earthworks Landscaping and Masonry LLC -->

# DESIGN.md — Earthworks Landscaping and Masonry LLC

archetype: modern-advisory
rationale: A homeowner vetting a Norwalk contractor has a short list of blunt questions: what do you build, what does it cost, how does the job run, do you come to my town, and will you leave a mess. modern-advisory answers them one band at a time, in plain Barlow and on panels of their own forest green, with the real figures ($28–$55 per sq ft, a 2-year workmanship warranty, a proposal in 3 business days) set large. That matches the owners' friendly, modern, clean brand and their "Honest Numbers" voice far better than a portfolio-first or a heritage look would.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [straight-talking, sturdy, neighbourly, exact]

typography:
  display: "Barlow"
  body: "Barlow"
  scale: 1.333
  notes: Barlow is the only family on the site. It uses one weight for headings (700) and one for body (400), set tight and left-aligned throughout. Display runs at clamp(2.75rem, 6vw, 5.25rem) with 1.02 leading and slightly negative tracking. h2 is 2.25rem and h3 is 1.35rem, both 700. Body is 1.125rem with 1.6 leading and a 62ch measure. Eyebrows (service group names, town names, day names) are 700 at 0.8rem, uppercase, with 0.14em tracking. Figures that matter (the phone number, "$28–$55 per square foot", "2-year", "3 business days") are 700 with tabular numerals, one size step above their surrounding text. Nothing is set below 0.875rem.

palette:
  primary: "#c50613"
  secondary: "#15431b"
  accent: "#acbdad"
  ground: "#f4f2ec"
  surface: "#e5eae2"
  ink: "#10251a"
  muted: "#4b5b4e"
  border: "#c7cfc4"
  application: >
    Secondary forest green (#15431b) is the structural colour. It carries the hero statement block,
    the process band, the closing contact band and the footer. All text on green is ground (#f4f2ec,
    about 10:1).

    Primary red (#c50613) is reserved for action. It appears on "Get a Free Estimate" buttons with
    white text (about 6:1), on the phone number as a link on the light ground (about 5.5:1), on the
    offer band's top rule, on the emergency-calls line and on the blog sidebar's phone link. Red is never used as text on green, where
    it fails.

    Accent sage (#acbdad) is graphic only and never carries text anywhere, because it measures about
    2.7:1 on green and 3.7:1 on the ground. It is used for the rules and step connector on the green
    band, the underline beneath eyebrows on green, and the 4px rule that divides bands.

    The ground is a warm stone-dust off-white and the surface a sage-tinted step up. Ink is the brand
    green pushed nearly to black (about 14:1 on ground). Muted is a green-grey that passes about 6.4:1
    on ground and 5.9:1 on surface. Focus rings are ground-coloured on green and ink-coloured on light
    grounds.

    These neutrals are bluestone dust, moss and wet mulch. They belong to a crew that lays stone and
    plants beds, not to any brand.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: supporting
  card_usage: none
  mobile: The hero statement block stacks beneath the image, which crops to 4:5 rather than sitting behind text, and the display type drops to 2.75rem. The service groups collapse to a single column of eyebrow-plus-line entries. The process runs vertically with the sage connector on the left. The gallery sample becomes a free-scroll horizontal strip cropped at the right edge. A round, red floating call button (3.5rem, a white phone icon only) appears on mobile only, fixed at the bottom-left so it stays clear of the accessibility widget's corner. It is a tel: link to 203-685-7355, with aria-label "Call or text 203-685-7355".

redirects: []

composition: >
  A homeowner's fear with a contractor is the number and the mess, not the portfolio. So this
  homepage wins on plain terms: the one real price they publish, the fixed written proposal, their
  own crew, a clean site every night, and a phone they answer themselves. Their photographs prove it
  can be done well; they are not asked to carry the case alone.

  The breadth of the work is sampled here, not listed. That means eight service groups, a handful of
  photographs and four of twelve answers. Everything else is held back for /services, /gallery and
  /contact.

  Every band answers exactly one question and says so in its heading. None of them says what the
  company believes.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Say what they do, "Stonework and Green Spaces Built to Outlive the Mortgage", as a Norwalk firm's promise. Make a site walk or a call the only next move.
    spec: >
      The supplied hero photograph (hero.backgroundImage) sits beside a forest-green (#15431b)
      statement block. They split asymmetrically at roughly 58/42, image-heavy, and the block
      overlaps the image edge by a few rem.

      A small eyebrow above the headline reads "Norwalk · Fairfield County, CT". The tagline is set
      in the block at display size in ground colour. The business description, "designs, builds and
      maintains patios, walls, walkways and gardens for homes across Norwalk and the Gold Coast", sits
      beneath it as a one-line standfirst, also in ground colour.

      Under that go one red "Get a Free Estimate" button linking to contact.html and the phone number
      203-685-7355 as a ground-coloured tel: link. Do not overlay text on the image. Write the alt
      text from what the photograph actually shows.
  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: "2 of 4 story paragraphs plus 4 of 8 reasons, links to about.html"
    intent: Answer "who will actually be in my yard?" with Nicholas and Phoenix, their summer-job origin, more than 25 years of combined experience, and care "we would give our own".
    spec: >
      The first two paragraphs of their story go in a 60ch left-aligned column, under the h2 "Built
      on Hard Work. Driven by Craftsmanship.".

      Beside it, four of their reasons are set as plain typographic statements: "One Crew, Start to
      Finish", "Honest Numbers", "Clean Site, Every Night" and "We Answer Our Own Phone". Each has a
      bold title and one line of their copy, with hairline rules in #c7cfc4 between them. There are
      no icons, no boxes and no numbering.

      A text link, "Our story →", goes to about.html. The about page carries all four paragraphs,
      their "Why Homeowners Keep Calling Back" passage and the eight reasons in the same typographic
      treatment.
  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "8 service groups of 32 services, each group name with its one-line description only, links to services.html"
    intent: Answer "can one company do all of it?" Their "two trades, one crew" reach runs from stone and drainage to lawn and snow, shown without turning the homepage into a thirty-two-line list.
    spec: >
      The section is headed "Services", with their line "Because we build the stone and plant the
      garden, the grades, drainage and sight lines all agree with each other." beneath it.

      All eight group names are set as uppercase eyebrows. Each one carries one sentence from their
      services-page description, for example Drainage & Grading: "French drains, dry wells, catch
      basins and regrading that pushes water away from your foundation." Use two columns of four on
      desktop with hairline rules between rows. Use no cards, no icons and no numbering, because
      these groups have no order.

      A link goes to services.html. There, every group gets its full description and all four named
      services. No per-item prices appear anywhere, because none exist.
  - id: pricing
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Answer the question every homeowner is afraid to ask, using the only real price they publish, and tie it to their fixed-written-proposal promise.
    spec: >
      A single from-band on surface (#e5eae2), left-aligned. "$28–$55 per square foot" is set at
      display size in ink, with the eyebrow "Most Norwalk stone patios" above it.

      Beneath it, in muted text, sit what changes the price (stone, base depth, grading, access) and
      the line "a fixed written price after a site visit — no hourly surprises". A 4px sage rule sits
      at the top edge. No other price is stated or implied.
  - id: film
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Let the visitor watch a real Norwalk job come together before they read about process, backing the offerings list with footage rather than claims.
    spec: >
      This is a forest-green band (on-green) placed directly after #offerings and before #gallery,
      matching the old site's order, where "Earthworks in Motion" followed the services. It uses
      the eyebrow "Featured Film", the h2 "Earthworks in Motion" and the standfirst "Stone, soil and
      steel — a look at how a Norwalk property comes together from first cut to final sweep."

      The video sits in a 16:9 frame up to 64rem wide, on black with a hairline border. It uses
      object-fit: contain, because the footage is shot upright. The poster is the bluestone fire-pit
      patio (Kora image aax9ez), under a light ink wash with a square forest-green play button with a
      ground border, the same button as on the gallery clips. A bottom gradient bar reads "Norwalk,
      CT" on the left and "1:27" on the right.

      The video uses preload="none", so nothing downloads until Play is pressed. Clicking Play hides
      the overlay and bar, turns on native controls and plays with sound. If playback fails, the
      overlay comes back. The file is the old site's earthworks-motion.mp4 (1:27, with audio),
      uploaded to Kora and served from stream.mux.com at 480p. A local copy is in docs/videos. The
      band carries VideoObject JSON-LD. The styles live in src/input.css under "Featured film".

      Known issue: the film's opening title card (about the first 10 seconds) shows the old number
      (203) 858-1773, which conflicts with the rule that only 203-685-7355 appears.
  - id: gallery
    priority: supporting
    show: "5 of the gallery photos on the homepage, chosen for variety of subject, links to gallery.html (which holds all 33 with filters)"
    intent: Let the work back up the terms. A visitor should see that the stone sits true and the beds look intentional.
    spec: >
      Five images from the SITE CONTENT gallery run as an uneven horizontal band at mixed widths, with
      a 2px ground-coloured gap. There are no card frames, no shadows and no uniform grid. The builder
      chooses the five by looking at them, for the widest range of subject.

      Captions are written only from what each photo visibly shows, in small muted text. A "See our
      work →" link goes to gallery.html.

      Each strip photo is wrapped in a .lightbox-open button (zoom-in cursor) and carries data-cat
      and a descriptive alt (the same wording as on gallery.html). It opens the same lightbox as the
      gallery page: counter, category, caption, prev/next, arrow keys, swipe, Esc or click outside
      to close, and focus returned to the photo. On the homepage, prev/next steps through the five
      strip photos. The lightbox styles are shared in src/input.css ("Lightbox"), and each page has
      its own small script.

      On gallery.html, 33 project photographs appear in a masonry arrangement (one column on mobile,
      two on tablet, three on desktop), with a 2px gap and each photo at its natural aspect ratio.
      The set is the 31 gallery photos from the old earthworksct.com/gallery (not its Before & After
      section) plus two Kora gallery images that were not on the old site: the sunlit tree-ring lawn
      (8mc96v) and the striped backyard lawn (qf2dh1). All are Kora-hosted WebP files. Ten reuse URLs
      the site already had, and 21 were uploaded for the gallery. Local copies and a full manifest
      are in the project's docs/gallery folder.

      Four filter buttons sit above the grid: All (33), Masonry (8), Landscaping (20) and Outdoor
      Living (5). They are square, uppercase, 700-weight buttons with a hairline border. The active
      one is filled forest green with ground text; red is not used here, because red is reserved for
      "Get a Free Estimate". Each figure carries data-cat="masonry|landscaping|outdoor-living". A
      small inline script toggles [hidden] on the figures, sets aria-pressed on the buttons and
      announces the count in a polite live region. Without JavaScript, all 33 photos show.

      Each photo has a caption (category eyebrow plus a description of what the photo shows) on a
      green-to-transparent gradient. It appears on hover or focus, and it always shows on touch
      screens. The first six images load eagerly and the rest lazily. The CollectionPage JSON-LD
      lists all 33 image URLs.

      Every photo is wrapped in a button (aria-haspopup="dialog", zoom-in cursor) that opens a
      lightbox. The lightbox is a native modal <dialog id="lightbox"> on near-opaque forest-green ink.
      Its top bar holds a "3 / 8" counter and a square close button. The photo is centred with
      object-fit: contain, with its category eyebrow and description underneath. Square prev/next
      buttons sit at the sides on desktop and at the bottom corners on mobile.

      Prev/next, the arrow keys and a swipe step through only the photos the current filter shows,
      and wrap around at either end. Esc, the close button or a click outside the photo closes it,
      and focus returns to the photo that opened it. Page scroll is locked while it is open, and the
      neighbouring photos are preloaded. The viewer uses the same square, hairline-bordered button
      language as the mobile nav. There is no red in it.

      Beneath the grid sits the Transformations band (#transformations). It is on surface with a
      4px sage top rule, the eyebrow "Transformations", the h2 "Before & After", and the line "Drag
      the handle across each project to see the same property before we started and after our
      crew finished." Four before/after slider cards follow, in two columns from 900px and one
      column below that:
      - Backyard Lawn Renovation, Norwalk
      - Front Entry Walkway, Rowayton
      - Failing Timber Wall Rebuild, Westport
      - Backyard Patio Build, Darien

      Each slider is a 3:2 frame. The after photo is the base layer, and the before photo sits on
      top, clipped with clip-path from the left to --pos. A 2px ground-coloured divider carries a
      square forest-green handle with a ground border and ‹ › arrows. Square "Before" (ink) and
      "After" (forest green) tags sit in the top corners. No red is used, because red stays
      reserved for action.

      An invisible, full-size <input type="range"> handles drag, click-to-jump, touch
      (touch-action: pan-y, so vertical page scroll still works) and keyboard (arrows, Home and
      End). Its aria-valuetext reads, for example, "40 percent before, 60 percent after". The frame
      shows the ink focus ring when the slider has keyboard focus. The slider starts at 50%.
      Below each frame come the town eyebrow, the project title as an h3 and one line of copy.

      The eight before/after photos come from the Before & After section of the old
      earthworksct.com/gallery. They were uploaded to Kora as WebP, and local copies and a manifest
      are in docs/transformations. The CollectionPage JSON-LD image list includes them.

      After Transformations comes the On Site band (#on-site) on the ground colour. It has the
      eyebrow "On Site", the h2 "Watch the Work" and the line "Short clips from recent Norwalk and
      Westport projects." Below it are two video cards in the same two-column grid as the sliders:
      - Masonry: "Setting Stone by Hand" ("Every course checked for level, every joint packed. This
        is a wall being built to sit still for forty winters.")
      - Landscaping: "A Finished Property" ("Grades that drain, beds that read as intentional, and a
        lawn thick enough to walk barefoot on.")

      Each clip sits in a 16:9 frame. Its poster is an existing Kora image: rd92r8 (stone setting)
      for the masonry clip and 8mc96v (the sunlit lawn) for the landscaping clip. Over the poster is a
      full-frame play button: a square forest-green icon with a ground border and a light ink wash.
      It is not red, to match the slider handles. The <video> tags use preload="none", so nothing
      downloads until the visitor presses Play. They are muted, looped and playsinline.

      Clicking Play hides the overlay, turns on native controls and starts the clip. It also pauses
      the other clip, so only one plays at a time. If playback fails, the overlay comes back. The
      videos are the old site's two clips (5 seconds each, silent), uploaded to Kora, which serves
      them from stream.mux.com. Local copies are in docs/videos. The page carries VideoObject
      JSON-LD for both.
  - id: process
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Answer "what happens after I call?" with Site Walk, Design & Price (proposal usually in 3 days), Build (the foreman texts progress photos) and Walkthrough (warranty registered).
    spec: >
      The four steps sit on the forest-green band, horizontally on desktop and vertically on mobile.
      Numbering 01–04 is correct here because the order is real.

      Each step has a title and one line of their copy, all in ground colour. The steps are joined by
      a thin sage connector rule. The same treatment is repeated on services.html.
  - id: reviews
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Let two real customers confirm the terms on punctuality, tidiness and fair pricing.
    spec: >
      One sentence from Dee R's review is pulled at h2 size across a narrow left-aligned measure:
      "They showed up on time, worked efficiently, and left the property spotless when they were
      finished." Her full text sits beneath it at body size.

      Melissa Robinson's review follows at body size. Attribution for both is an uppercase eyebrow.
      There are no star graphics, no carousel and no avatars. Only these two reviews appear.
  - id: offers
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Surface the two new-customer offers plainly, as seasonal savings, without urgency theatre.
    spec: >
      A single band on ground with a red top rule holds two left-aligned text columns:
      - "Spring Cleanup Special: 10% off all spring cleanups for new customers"
      - "Leaf Cleanup Season: new customers save up to $75 off their first leaf cleanup"

      Each column lists its included work in one line and ends with "Call or text 203-685-7355" as a
      red tel: link. No end dates are stated, because none exist.
  - id: service_area
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Answer "do they come to me?" at a glance.
    spec: >
      The line "Based in Norwalk, working throughout Fairfield County" is followed by the towns from
      their FAQ as a single run of uppercase eyebrows separated by middle dots: Westport, Wilton,
      Darien, New Canaan, Stamford, Fairfield, Weston, Greenwich.

      Then comes "If you're within about 30 minutes of our yard, we can be on site." There is no map
      here.
  - id: faq
    priority: supporting
    show: "4 of 12, chosen for the worries that stop people calling, links to contact.html"
    intent: Clear the last objections: are you licensed and insured, is the estimate free, how long does it take, and what is the warranty.
    spec: >
      Four questions are set as two-column Q&A on desktop and stacked on mobile, with hairlines
      between them. The link "All twelve answers →" goes to contact.html.

      On contact.html, all 12 appear as an accordion under their heading "Answers Before You Call".
  - id: hours_location
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Show they keep contractor's hours and pick up for storms.
    spec: >
      An aligned day/time table uses tabular numerals: Mon–Fri 07:00–18:00, Sat 08:00–14:00, Sun
      Closed. Beneath it, "Emergency storm calls anytime" is set in red on the light ground.

      Beside the table sits the address exactly as written: 10 Platt St, Norwalk, CT 06855. The SITE
      CONTENT map embed appears on contact.html only.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Get the site walk booked, by form or by phone, whichever the visitor prefers.
    spec: >
      On the homepage, this is a closing band on forest green. It carries "Ready to Build Something
      That Lasts?", the phone number 203-685-7355 at display size as a ground-coloured tel: link, a
      red "Get a Free Estimate" button to contact.html, and the address in small ground-coloured
      type.

      On contact.html, a split-form layout puts a quote form on one side:
      - form_type is "quote"
      - fields are name, phone, email, town, project type (their options: Patio or Walkway, Retaining
        Wall, Outdoor Kitchen / Fireplace, Planting & Garden Design, Drainage & Grading, Lawn
        Maintenance, Other) and project details
      - project details maps to form_data.message
      - it posts to /api/v1/public/forms/submit with lazily loaded reCAPTCHA using the provided key
      - the KORA_SITE_CONFIG block appears on every page
      - inputs have an explicit ground background and ink text

      The details column holds the phone, address, hours, and the Facebook and Yelp links. No business
      email appears anywhere, because none exists.

  - id: blog
    priority: supporting
    show: "all 6 articles on blog.html; one article per blog-<slug>.html page"
    intent: Answer the questions homeowners search before they call (patio material, failing walls, plants, standing water, lighting, spring checks) in the crew's plain voice, and turn each answer into a site walk.
    spec: >
      Blog is a first-class page. It sits in the header nav, the mobile nav and the footer "Pages"
      list, after Gallery and before the "Get a Free Estimate" button. It is marked active with
      aria-current="page" on blog.html and every article page.

      blog.html has a band-tight hero (eyebrow "Field Notes · Norwalk, CT", display h1 "The Earthworks
      Blog", and the standfirst "What we've learned building stone and gardens in Connecticut
      weather."). Below it, the six articles are listed newest first in a .post-list grid: three
      columns on desktop, two on tablet, one on mobile. Each entry has a 4:3 image, a category eyebrow,
      the title as an h2 link, the excerpt in muted text, date and read time, and "Read the article →".
      Entries are separated by hairline top rules, not cards: no shadows and no rounded containers.

      Each article is a flat root file, blog-<slug>.html, served at /blog-<slug>. Posts are not in a
      /blog/ folder, because every page must load assets/styles.css relatively and no internal href
      may start with "/". An article page has breadcrumbs (Home / Blog / category), a category eyebrow,
      the headline as the page's only h1 (.display .post-title, capped at 4rem), the excerpt as the
      standfirst, and the byline "By the Earthworks crew", date and read time. Then comes a full-bleed
      featured image (4:3 on mobile, 21:9 on desktop). The body is set in .prose at 68ch, with h2
      subheads, square sage-marked bullets and numbered lists.

      A sticky sidebar (.post-aside, desktop only; it stacks below the article on mobile) holds a
      "Free site walk" block with the red tel: link and a "Get a Free Estimate" button, and "More from
      the blog" linking the other five articles. Every blog page ends with the green contact band
      "Questions About Your Own Yard?".

      Each article carries BlogPosting JSON-LD (author and publisher are #business, with a
      BreadcrumbList). blog.html carries Blog JSON-LD listing all six posts. og:type is "article" on
      posts and "website" on the index. The og:image is the post's featured image.

      Article images are the supplied Kora-hosted WebP files. Three are shared with the gallery
      (bluestone patio, retaining wall, planting), and the other three were uploaded for the blog
      (drainage, lighting, spring). The blog hero image is gallery image 7uqth5. Alt text describes
      what each photo shows.

      The only phone number is 203-685-7355. Posts reuse the site's published facts
      ($28–$55 per square foot, a proposal within 3 business days, permits and engineering handled
      for walls over four feet) and state no other prices.

      To add a post, copy an existing blog-<slug>.html. Then add it to the top of the blog.html list
      and its Blog JSON-LD, to every other post's "More from the blog" list, to llms.txt, to
      sitemap.xml and to .kora/site-index.md.

avoid:
  - The stat counters from their old site ("529+ Years", "36,504 Projects", "1,711,927 sq ft", "2,467%"). They are impossible and would destroy trust. Do not animate or count up any number.
  - Any years-in-business figure other than "more than 25 years of combined experience" from their own story. The old site's conflicting "21 Years" and "two decades" claims do not get a headline.
  - The old phone number (203) 858-1773. Only 203-685-7355 appears anywhere.
  - Any business email address, mailto link or "email us" line.
  - Links to pages on the old earthworksct.com site, including the old /contact and /gallery CTA URLs. Every link points at this site's own pages.
  - The word "Menu" anywhere. The section is "Services".
  - A three-icon "Masonry / Design / Lawn Care" card row, which the old homepage had and every landscaper has.
  - Numbering on the service groups. 01–04 is used only on the four-step process.
  - A hero or band headline that states a belief ("we believe every property deserves…") instead of what they build.
  - Drop shadows, rounded card containers and serif display type.
  - Stock photos of lawns, seedlings in hands, or a smiling crew. Only the supplied image URLs are used.
  - The Facebook feed embed. None of that content exists here. (The blog, the "Watch the Work" clips and the "Featured Film" are not in this list: all three are part of the site. See the blog section, the On Site band on gallery.html and the film section on the homepage.)
  - Blog posts in a /blog/ subfolder, absolute "/blog/..." links, or a second h1 on an article page.
  - Before/after sliders anywhere other than the gallery page's Transformations band, and round or red slider handles. The four sliders live only on gallery.html.
  - The Maureen D. and Alec Lasky quotes from the old site. Only the two reviews in SITE CONTENT appear.
  - Sage (#acbdad) as a text colour, or red (#c50613) text on the green band.
  - Emoji, "🔥", "limited availability" and exclamation-mark urgency carried over from the Facebook posts.
